analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset()` calls `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, &offset)` on the c-offsets buffer returned by `get_coffsets()` without passing/validating the actual buffer length. `blosc_getitem()` (non-ctx variant) internally uses `INT32_MAX` as `srcsize`, so malformed/truncated attacker-controlled offset chunks can make `_blosc_getitem`/`blosc_d` read past the real buffer and crash in `sw32_` while parsing stream headers. The missing size-aware validation is in frame offset retrieval, not in the crashing `sw32_` helper.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, attacker input is opened as an in-memory frame via `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe`, then `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` triggers `frame_decompress_chunk -> frame_get_lazychunk -> get_coffset`. A crafted frame with an invalid/truncated `coffsets` chunk (or inconsistent metadata causing short coffsets data) reaches `get_coffset`; because it uses size-unbounded `blosc_getitem`, decompression of that coffsets entry performs OOB reads and segfaults. Trigger requires successful enough frame parsing to reach chunk-offset lookup plus malformed coffsets content/length.
